{{Current events|year=2023|month=01|day=29|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Eastern Ukraine campaign]]
****Forces of the [[Wagner Group]] say that they have captured the village of Blahodatne, north of [[Bakhmut]]. However, [[Ukraine]] rejects the claim and says that it repelled the attack. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2023/01/29/ukraine-says-repelled-attack-near-blahodatne-russias-wagner-claims-control-a80073 (AFP via ''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[Southern Ukraine campaign]]
****[[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] [[shell (projectile)|shell]] the city of [[Kherson]], killing three people, injuring six others, and damaging a hospital, school, and bus station. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2023-01-29/three-killed-by-russian-shelling-of-kherson-officials (Reuters via U.S. News & World Report)]
*[[Islamist insurgency in the Sahel]]
**[[Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso]]
***The governor of [[Comoé Province]] reports that 15 [[corpse]]s, who were among 24 passengers of two [[minibus]]es that departed the provincial capital of [[Banfora]] when suspected [[jihadist]]s hijacked the buses in [[Linguekoro]] and coerced the passengers to walk to [[Mangodara]], were discovered near Linguekoro. The governor also reports that 15 other passengers had been abducted. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/overseas/01/31/23/suspected-jihadists-kill-28-in-troubled-burkina-faso (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian civil war]]
***Unidentified [[warplane]]s, suspected to be [[Israeli Air Force|Israeli]], strike a convoy of [[Iran]]ian trucks that entered [[Syria]] from [[Iraq]] through the [[Al-Qa'im border crossing]]. At least six trucks are believed to have been destroyed. There are no immediate reports of casualties. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/warplanes-said-to-strike-convoy-of-iranian-militia-trucks-on-syria-iraq-border/ (''Times of Israel'')]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**An 18-year-old [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] man is shot dead by a group of [[Israelis|Israeli]] [[civilian]]s near the [[Israeli settlement|settlement]] of [[Kedumim]], in the [[West Bank]]. In a separate incident, a Palestinian civilian home is [[Arson|set on fire]] by settlers. The occupants were not there at the time of the attack. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/1/29/israeli-guards-kill-palestinian-near-west-bank-settlement (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Lasbela bus crash]]
**At least 41 people are killed and two others are injured when a bus falls off a bridge and catches fire in [[Lasbela District]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/bus-crash-southern-pakistan-kills-41-local-media-2023-01-29/ (Reuters)]
*[[2022–23 South-West Indian Ocean cyclone season]]
**The death toll from [[Cyclone Cheneso]]'s landfall in [[Madagascar]] has increased to 25, with 21 others still missing. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/overseas/01/29/23/tens-of-thousands-homeless-after-madagascar-tropical-storm (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
*[[Tanda Dam incident]]
**Ten children are killed and eleven other people are injured when a boat [[capsize]]s at the [[Tanda Dam]] in [[Kohat District]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/ten-children-killed-in-northwest-pakistan-boat-capsize-police-01674978607 (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
*At least 22 people are killed and 21 injured when a bus crashes near [[Dassa-Zoumé]], [[Collines Department]], [[Benin]]. [https://www.trtworld.com/africa/benin-bus-crash-kills-more-than-a-dozen-65018 (TRT World)]
*At least nine people are killed when a container falls from a truck onto a commercial bus in [[Lagos]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://guardian.ng/news/container-falls-off-truck-in-lagos-crushes-9-passengers-to-death/ (''The Guardian Nigeria'')]
*An [[avalanche]] on [[Mount Norikura]] in [[Nagano Prefecture]], [[Japan]], kills two people, including American skier [[Kyle Smaine]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-64451744 (BBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Attack on the Azerbaijani Embassy in Tehran]]
**[[Azerbaijan–Iran relations]]
***[[Azerbaijan]] suspends [[diplomat]]ic activities at its [[Diplomatic mission|embassy]] in [[Tehran]] after accusing [[Iran]] of failing to ensure the security of its embassy staff. The Azerbaijani [[Consul (representative)|consulate general]] in [[Tabriz]] continues to operate routinely. [https://tass.com/world/1568657 (TASS)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2023 Gqeberha shooting]]
**Eight people are killed and three others are injured in a [[mass shooting]] at a [[birthday party]] in [[Gqeberha]], [[Eastern Cape]], [[South Africa]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/gunmen-kill-eight-at-birthday-party-in-south-africa-police-101675057723706.html (AFP via ''Hindustan Times'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Liechtenstein constitutional referendum]]
**Voters in [[Liechtenstein]] reject a proposed ban on [[casino]]s. The proposal, which [[Hans-Adam II, Prince of Liechtenstein|Prince Hans-Adam II]] opposed, was rejected by around 73 percent of voters. [https://www.euronews.com/2023/01/29/place-your-bets-liechtenstein-gambles-on-keeping-casinos (Euronews)]
*[[2022–23 Tunisian parliamentary election]]
**[[Tunisians]] head to [[Polling station|the polls]] to elect the members of the third [[Assembly of the Representatives of the People]] in a [[Run-off election|run-off]]. The [[Elections in Tunisia|electoral board]] reports a [[voter turnout]] of 11.3 percent as most opposition parties boycott the election. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20230129-tunisians-to-vote-in-second-round-of-poll-for-defanged-parliament (AFP via RFI)]
*[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|UK prime minister]] [[Rishi Sunak]] dismisses [[Nadhim Zahawi]] as [[chairman of the Conservative Party]] and [[Minister without portfolio (United Kingdom)|minister without portfolio]] after Sunak's ethics adviser, [[Laurie Magnus (executive)|Laurie Magnus]], found that Zahawi had breached the [[Ministerial Code]] for failing to disclose a [[Pound sterling|£]]5 million tax penalty payment to [[HM Revenue and Customs]] while serving as [[Chancellor of the Exchequer]] under former prime minister [[Boris Johnson]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-64444265 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023 Australian Open – Men's singles]]
**[[Novak Djokovic]] defeats [[Stefanos Tsitsipas]] in the final, 6–3, 7–6<sup>(7–4)</sup>, 7–6<sup>(7–5)</sup>, to win the men's singles [[tennis]] title at the 2023 [[Australian Open]] in [[Melbourne]], tying him with [[Rafael Nadal]] for the most [[Grand Slam (tennis)|Grand Slam]]s in men's tennis history with 22. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/tennis/62998399 (BBC Sport)]
*[[2023 World Men's Handball Championship]]
**[[Denmark men's national handball team|Denmark]] defeats [[France men's national handball team|France]] 34–29 in the final to win the 2023 [[World Men's Handball Championship]] in [[Stockholm]], [[Sweden]]. Denmark becomes the first men's national [[handball]] team to win three consecutive world titles, having also won the [[2019 World Men's Handball Championship|2019]] and [[2021 World Men's Handball Championship|2021]] editions. [https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/denmark-beat-france-historic-third-handball-world-title-2023-01-29/ (Reuters)]
